Coding agents start every session from zero. [Harness Firmware](https://github.com/ryanportfolio/Harness-Firmware) is a set of files you add to a repository so Claude Code and Codex work from the project's own rules, memory and workflows. The agent loads a skill or a note only when the task calls for it, a second model reviews the work before you approve it, and what one session learns is written down for the next.

## What it does for your agent

### Token-efficient

Skills and project notes load only when a task needs them.

- `caveman` (always on): Replies drop filler and pleasantries and keep every technical detail, from the first message.
- `recall` (automatic): Before unfamiliar work, the agent reads the project notes that apply and skips the rest.

### Planned

Brainstorm, write the plan, and test alternatives before building.

- `/dare`: Takes the problem apart from first principles in four fresh passes: break it down, test each assumption, rebuild, check the result against reality.
- `/arena`: Runs several attempts in parallel, keeps the strongest as the base, and folds in the best parts of the rest.
- `/lab`: Builds a live prototype with controls, so you tune motion and layout by feel before anything is final.

### Audited

A second model reviews the work before you approve it.

- `/codex-review`: OpenAI's Codex, a different model family, reviews the diff. Each finding is checked against the code before anything changes.
- `/impartial-review`: Fresh agents that never saw the work review it.
- `/handoff-audit`: Writes an audit brief with exact scope and pass/fail checks that another session can run.

### Remembered

Decisions and pitfalls carry into the next session.

- `pitfalls.md` (auto-saved): A mistake that cost a retry gets written down, so the next session avoids it.
- `architecture.md` (auto-loaded): How the system fits together, in a plain file the agent reads before it changes an unfamiliar area.

### Production-ready

Long tasks run in audited rounds. Finished work gets polished and measured before it ships.

- `/wow-loop`: Reviews and repairs one piece against the goal, round after round, and keeps only changes that prove better.
- `/perf-loop`: Measures speed against a baseline, changes one thing, and measures again with an independent check.
- `/long-horizon`: Splits work too big for one context window into rounds. A fresh agent builds each round, a separate auditor checks the real files, and only work that passes moves forward.
- `/long-horizon-workflows`: Runs the same rounds through Claude Code's built-in workflows, with a fresh builder, an inspector and a panel of judges each round, written verdicts and a run journal.

### Self-improving

When a workflow stumbles, the fix goes into the skill itself.

- `/refine`: Traces the stumble to its cause and edits the skill, so the next run starts from the fix.

## Get started

Start a new repository with the firmware at [harnessfirmware.com/new](https://harnessfirmware.com/new).

The firmware itself lives in [ryanportfolio/Harness-Firmware](https://github.com/ryanportfolio/Harness-Firmware). Use it as a GitHub template, or copy its skills into a repository you already have.

## This repository

This repository is the source of [harnessfirmware.com](https://harnessfirmware.com). To run the site locally with Node.js, with nothing to install:

```sh
node site/server.mjs
```

Then open http://127.0.0.1:4348.
